summary: axe-core 4.13.0 (WCAG 2.1 A/AA) and keyboard-only traversal, driven by Playwright chromium against the application's own deployed URL: the mold's three page routes signed OUT, and the product itself — chat thread, ops centre, workflow builder — signed IN with a session this deployment minted. A route that answers 2xx and then renders no interactive control fails the row, and so does a signed-in surface that renders only the signed-out shell: nothing measured is never a pass.

requires.else: Install the browser this lane drives: npm i -g playwright && npx playwright install chromium.
Restore the vendored rule set: npm --prefix molds/mold_v1/testing/accessibility run vendor

checks.name: axe.wcag21aa

requires.else: This lane grades rendered pages, so the app has to be deployed first: python3 .claude/scripts/provision.py {app_id} --deploy

The deployed app did not serve this application on /, /onboard, /workspace — either it is not deployed, or the URL now answers with something that is not this mold (mold_v1 apps share one Vercel project). Redeploy it: python3 .claude/scripts/provision.py {app_id} --deploy

checks.why: A serious or critical WCAG 2.1 A/AA violation is a customer who cannot use the page at all: an unnamed button is invisible to a screen reader, and failing contrast is unreadable in daylight or with low vision.

This check grades the signed-in product (chat thread, ops centre, workflow builder), so it needs a session for it: sign in to the app as the factory's test identity, copy that browser's `fde-google-token` value out of localStorage, and re-run the lane with it in MOLD_V1_SESSION_TOKEN — step by step in molds/mold_v1/testing/accessibility/README.md, "Authenticated coverage". Until then this lane is `skipped`, never `pass`: it has not seen the product.

The session in MOLD_V1_SESSION_TOKEN is missing, expired, too close to expiry to outlast this check, or refused by this deployment, so this run would measure the signed-out shell instead of the product. Sign in to the app as the factory's test identity, copy that browser's `fde-google-token` value out of localStorage, and re-run the lane with it in MOLD_V1_SESSION_TOKEN — step by step in molds/mold_v1/testing/accessibility/README.md, "Authenticated coverage". Until then this check is `skipped` and so is the LANE: it is never `pass`, and never `fail` either — a stale credential is not a defect of the application.

checks.why: Signed out, this lane reaches a sign-in page and an empty shell — 2 to 9 controls, none of them the product. A green lane over that certifies nothing a customer uses. This is the check that grades the workspace they actually work in, and the first run of it found 20 serious contrast violations and a select with no name.

not_covered: Anything the session token cannot reach. The signed-in check grades four surfaces (chat thread, People, Audit trail, workflow builder); the data room, connectors, agents tabs and the ops-centre modal inside the chat shell are NOT graded, and neither is any state that needs a write (creating a workflow, sending a message) — this lane is read-only on the application it grades and every non-GET the browser attempts is aborted and counted.

The signed-in surface at all, whenever MOLD_V1_SESSION_TOKEN is absent, expired, too close to expiry to outlast the run, or refused by this deployment: session-live.py makes the check `skipped` before a browser opens, and the LANE is then `skipped`. It is never `pass` on the strength of the signed-out rows alone (mold_v1-040), and never `fail` — a stale credential is not a defect of the application.

Which identity's data is on screen. The lane measures the workspace the supplied session resolves to; a different role (member vs owner) renders different controls, and only the one supplied is graded.
Screen-reader output. axe-core checks the accessibility tree, not what NVDA/VoiceOver actually announces.
Best-practice and moderate/minor axe rules. They are printed in the detail column (for example landmark-one-main and region on /workspace) but do not fail the lane.
axe `incomplete` results, which need a human to judge them; the count is printed per route.
Colour rendering under a different theme or brand pack, zoom to 200%, reduced motion and forced-colors modes.

Routes that do not exist in this mold snapshot. The mold has three page routes (/, /onboard, /workspace); there is no /chat route — chat is rendered at /, and the ops-centre tabs are `?tab=` addresses on /workspace.

Whether the page served is THIS application's data. The precondition checks that the HTML carries this mold's own markers, which catches an undeployed URL and a URL now served by something else; it cannot tell two mold_v1 applications apart, because they render the same markup. A wrong-but-same-mold `production_url` is a provisioning defect, not one this lane can see.
